facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: The issuer's adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 623.6 million to USD 575.4 million, which gives net leverage of 5.12x and 5.50x. The add-backs the issuer applies rose from USD 46.4 million to USD 164.5 million, so USD 118.1 million of the USD 166.3 million fall in reported EBITDA reflects higher add-backs rather than lower adjusted earnings. The strongest contrary evidence is that the adjusted view flatters the latest figure: it keeps USD 64.1 million of tariff refund benefit recorded in the nine months to 2026-06-30, only about USD 11.0 million of which had been collected after quarter end, and excluding that benefit alone would put adjusted net leverage at 6.18x (Analyst Judgement, not an issuer figure). A fourth-quarter result without further add-backs would favour the adjusted view; further restructuring cost or a delay in refund collection would favour the reported one. Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C06; calculation C13

facts.text: Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was USD 173.4 million of cash plus USD 462.4 million undrawn on the revolving facility, USD 635.8 million in all, against USD 8.6 million of debt maturing within a year. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 137–138 - Medium: About 93% of cash at 2026-06-30 was held outside the U.S., and the company says repatriation could have adverse tax consequences or be subject to regulatory capital requirements, so the amount of cash readily available to the U.S. borrower and note issuers is not established and net debt subtracts all of it. A split of cash by entity and jurisdiction would close this. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 103 - Medium: Receivables sold without recourse are printed at fiscal year-ends only, so the interim balance and the trend of this off-balance-sheet funding are not established; supplier-financed obligations are printed at each date. The interim balance would close this. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 19 - Medium: The nine months to 2025-06-30 comparative includes out-of-period production credits recorded in the third quarter of fiscal 2025, so year-on-year comparisons of that period are distorted; the credits are shown as separate figures. The issuer's quarterly schedules let the credits be isolated. Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 41 - Low: Capital expenditure is printed as a total only, so maintenance and growth capex are not established and the free cash flow shown is not split between them. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3 - Low: No separate short-term investment balance is printed, since cash equivalents include marketable securities of three months or less, so no investment is added to or excluded from net debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 103 - Low: Source dashes in the statements (for example asset sale proceeds in fiscal 2025 and the third-quarter loss on extinguishment) are kept as missing rather than zero, which leaves component sums of those lines uncertified; reported totals remain usable. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3 - Low: Prior-year interim balance sheets are not supplied, so balance-sheet trends before 2025-09-30 other than the two fiscal year-ends are not available from the filings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3 - Low: No EBITDA figure is printed in the filed reports and no full-year fiscal 2025 EBITDA is printed in any release, so annual EBITDA is calculated from statement lines and checked against the printed quarters. Basis: EX99.1_2025-12-31_enr_enrpr123125-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 99–101 - Low: The issuer prints no operating income line, so EBIT is not calculable, and no consistent quantified operating series (volumes, distribution points or customer retention) or prior-year nine-month organic growth rate is printed; management gives only percentage contributions to organic growth. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 44 - Low: Fiscal 2024 and 2023 net sales by market were recast in the fiscal 2025 annual report; no market split is used here and totals are unchanged. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 113

facts.text: The strongest evidence for a higher risk level is that fiscal 2025 payouts of USD 176.8 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 63.2 million, in a year when net new debt financing was USD 155.9 million, which would be creditor-adverse if repeated without covenant limits that cannot be seen. The strongest evidence for a lower level is that fiscal 2026 payouts fell to 0.67 times free cash flow, USD 90.0 million of term loan was prepaid, maturities were extended to 2030, 2032 and 2033, and no sponsor, fee or related-party leakage appears in the supplied pages. The view would move to low if the fiscal 2026 annual report shows continued repayment and the executed documents show tight restricted-payment limits, and to high if payouts again exceed free cash flow or the supplemental indentures show weaker note priority. facts.text: Two financings in fiscal 2025 reshaped the debt without changing leverage. In March 2025 the credit agreement was amended and restated, extending the USD 760 million senior secured term loan to 2032 and the USD 500 million revolving facility to 2030 for debt issuance costs of USD 8.0 million. In September 2025 the company issued USD 400.0 million of 6.00% senior notes due 2033, guaranteed on an unsecured basis by certain domestic restricted subsidiaries, redeemed USD 300 million of 6.50% notes due 2027 with a premium of USD 4.9 million, and added USD 100.0 million to the term loan to repay revolver borrowings. Together the fiscal 2025 financings cost USD 13.6 million of debt issuance costs plus the premium, and extended the note maturity wall at a lower coupon. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a weak assessment is that earnings still cover interest and liquidity is adequate. Trailing adjusted EBITDA is 4.03 times the next twelve months' contractual interest of USD 142.8 million and reported EBITDA is 2.88 times, no note matures before the 2028 notes, the company refinanced successfully in 2025, capital intensity is low at 2.24% of sales, and about USD 53.1 million of the tariff refund is still to be collected. The production credit, expected at USD 55 million to USD 65 million a year until its phase-out begins in 2030, is recurring rather than one-off, and the guided fourth quarter needs only USD 4.6 million more adjusted EBITDA than the prior-year quarter, against USD 7.0 million to USD 17.0 million of programme benefit still to be realised. The view would move toward average if fiscal 2026 results confirm adjusted EBITDA of USD 580 million or more with add-backs below USD 164.5 million, if adjusted net leverage returns to the 5.12x of 2025-09-30, if the refund is collected in cash and if the 2028 notes are refinanced early near the 6.00% coupon of the 2033 notes. It would weaken if adjusted EBITDA falls short of USD 580 million, add-backs rise again, free cash flow fails to cover the dividend as in fiscal 2025, revolver borrowings rise above USD 30.0 million, or the 2028 notes approach their final twelve months unrefinanced. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Energizer makes and sells household and specialty batteries, portable lights and auto care products under the Energizer, Eveready and Rayovac brands, with Varta in Latin America and Asia Pacific, and Armor All, STP and A/C PRO in auto care. Sales go through mass merchants, food, drug, hardware, automotive and e-commerce channels, and about 40% of fiscal 2025 sales arose outside the United States. In the nine months to 2026-06-30, Batteries & Lights was 78.03% of segment net sales and Auto Care 21.97%. Battery demand follows device usage, consumer demographics and disasters and auto care follows the car parc and miles driven, so cash flow is needs-based but seasonal: batteries peak around the first fiscal quarter and auto care in the third and fourth, which makes working capital swing within the year. The business model supports debt service through steady replacement demand and low capital intensity, but it gives little pricing protection, because the sources give no backlog or customer contract term and sales depend on retailer shelf space. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Energizer is a listed Missouri corporation with no sponsor or controlling holder named and a dispersed holder base, so the financial-policy question is the Board's discretion over dividends and repurchases, which the company says depends on debt service obligations and covenants. Takeover protections in the articles and Missouri law make a leveraged change of control less likely. The credit agreement is guaranteed by certain domestic restricted subsidiaries, who also guarantee the 2033 notes on an unsecured basis; the guarantee scope of the 2028 and 2029 notes and the identity of the guarantors are not stated, and about 40% of sales and 93% of cash sit abroad, so claims on those assets may rank behind local liabilities. All figures are for Energizer Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries consolidated: no parent is named, so no parent figure is used, and Energizer Gamma Acquisition B.V. is a party to the euro notes' indenture without separate statements in the supplied documents. The ownership percentages, board committees and pay are in a proxy statement that is not supplied. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is recurring in the sense that batteries and auto care products are replaced or topped up, but it is price-sensitive and moves with promotion. Organic growth was 0.7% in fiscal 2025, made of volume growth of 1.5% and pricing declines of 0.8%, then fell 2.3% in the nine months to 2026-06-30 as volumes fell 2.1% on softer U.S. consumer demand and a storm-heavy prior year, with pricing down 0.2%. The third quarter turned positive, with organic sales up 2.7% from volume gains of 4.1% against pricing declines of 1.4%, so recent volume has been bought with promotion. North America, 52.76% of nine-month sales, fell 2.93% in the nine months though it grew 4.31% in the third quarter. The largest customer, at 12.8% of fiscal 2025 sales, and the retailer trend toward private label limit pricing power; the expired acquired brand licence cut third-quarter sales by USD 17.2 million. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: The sources give no fixed-versus-variable cost split, but cost of products sold was 63.08% of net sales in the nine months to 2026-06-30, SG&A 19.09% and advertising 5.1%, and the plant network is being reshaped under Project Momentum. Principal inputs are manganese dioxide, zinc, silver, nickel, lithium, steel and plastic for batteries and refrigerant R-134a for auto care; zinc hedges cover a notional of about USD 24 million against nine-month cost of products sold of USD 1,360.3 million, so on the information supplied most input-cost and tariff exposure is not hedged and passes to margin unless priced. Margins have not been defended: adjusted gross margin fell 2.7 percentage points on mix, input cost and production inefficiency, partly offset by the tariff refund. Cost flexibility exists in advertising, which fell 6.55% to USD 109.9 million, and in the programme's savings of about USD 15 million in the first nine months of its fourth year, but both are modest against the margin loss. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital intensity is low: capital expenditure was 2.24% of trailing net sales, and USD 60 million to USD 70 million is planned for fiscal 2026, down from USD 75 million to USD 85 million in the annual report, of which USD 25 million to USD 35 million is Project Momentum, which shows capital expenditure being flexed. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is intense and mature: the annual report calls the categories highly competitive, names competitors with greater resources and describes aggressive competition in the United States, so promotion and price investment cap margin recovery and weigh on cash flow. The threat of new entrants comes mainly from retailers' private label and from e-commerce and discounters, which the company expects to shift consumption between channels and which can force lower prices or loss of distribution. Substitutes are not described beyond private label, so no further credit effect is claimed. Buyer power is high: customers frequently seek pricing concessions and better trade terms, one retailer is 12.8% of sales, and retailer consolidation is cited, which supports the view that pricing is a structural margin headwind. Supplier power is moderate: raw materials are commodities with fluctuating prices but available from several sources, and the company hedges part of its zinc, so supplier power matters mainly through tariffs and input-cost swings. facts.label: Macro, policy and trade factors
facts.text: Policy and trade factors are material to credit; social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. On the political and regulatory side, the Supreme Court held the IEEPA tariffs invalid on 2026-02-20, which created a refund claim of about USD 64 million that lifted nine-month earnings by USD 64.1 million while only about USD 11.0 million had been received after quarter end and the timeline for the rest is unclear; replacement tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on some trading partners keep the cost exposure open. The federal production credit, expected at USD 55 million to USD 65 million a year, depends on continuing regulation and phases out from 2030, so a change in policy would cut earnings directly. On the economic side, U.S. consumer demand is soft, currency moves reduce margin when local currencies weaken because much product cost is dollar-linked, and floating-rate debt of USD 791.9 million carries interest-rate risk. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Strengths. Scale of about USD 3.0bn of trailing sales with established brands supports retailer access and cash generation; capital intensity of 2.24% of sales leaves cash for debt service; liquidity of USD 635.8 million is adequate against near-term obligations; the 2025 refinancing extended the bank facilities to 2030 and 2032 and issued 2033 notes; and the dividend was held while USD 90.0 million of term loan was prepaid. Weaknesses. Adjusted EBITDA is falling and carries add-backs of USD 164.5 million; margins are eroding under mix, promotion and input costs; USD 2,117.2 million of notes mature in 2028 and 2029; batteries and North America dominate sales; and intangible assets exceed equity. Opportunities. Collection of the remaining tariff refund of about USD 53.1 million, early refinancing before the notes become current, savings from the fourth year of Project Momentum and growth in e-commerce and Auto Care distribution could each improve credit quality. Threats. A retailer moving shelf space to private label, loss of the production credit, higher replacement tariffs, rising floating-rate cost as the swap steps down, and an adverse outcome in the consolidated antitrust class actions, for which no accrual is recorded, could each weaken it. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: The main supports are liquidity with no maturity before the 2028 notes, low capital intensity, a demonstrated ability to refinance in 2025 and a policy shift toward debt repayment in fiscal 2026. The main constraints are leverage of 7.70x reported and 5.50x adjusted, falling earnings quality with 28.59% of adjusted EBITDA made of add-backs, volatile free cash flow and the 65.10% concentration of maturities in two years. The trend is negative on earnings and neutral on debt: net debt is USD 33.3 million lower than at 2025-09-30 but USD 47.8 million above its level at 2025-12-31, and trailing reported EBITDA is 28.81% lower than in fiscal 2025 and the company has cut its guide. The datapoints that would make the opinion more definitive are the fiscal 2026 year-end results, covenant levels and springing-maturity terms, the share of cash available to the U.S. borrowers, interim cash interest paid, and a rating or market spread; none is supplied. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months, the supports are the guided fourth-quarter profit recovery, collection of the remaining tariff refund, the savings and tariff mitigation from the fourth programme year, and production credit of USD 55 million to USD 65 million a year; the pressures are flat-to-lower organic sales, promotional pricing, replacement tariffs, restructuring guided at USD 80 million to USD 95 million of cost for fiscal 2026, interest expense guided at USD 150 million to USD 160 million, the roll-off of the interest rate swap that fixes the benchmark on USD 500.0 million and steps down by USD 100.0 million each December to 2027-12-22, and the start of the 2028 refinancing. Over three to five years the maturity wall of 2028 and 2029 comes first, then the revolver in 2030, the production credit phase-out from 2030, and the term loan in 2032 and notes in 2033. Rayovac amortisation begins on 2026-07-01 but is non-cash. At the guided figures and with net debt held at its 2026-06-30 level, adjusted net leverage would be 5.45x and reported 7.42x, so the guide implies no deleveraging from earnings. Each pressure works through margin and refinancing cost, not liquidity, in the first two years. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with a continued consumer slowdown and retailer promotion, set against higher replacement tariffs, which holds organic sales below the flat-to-down fourth-quarter guide. The first operational break is gross margin: adjusted gross margin would stay below the 39.2% of the nine months as mix and promotion offset savings, and the tariff refund of USD 64.1 million and the production credit stop supporting earnings. Financially, trailing adjusted EBITDA would fall to USD 456.3 million and adjusted net leverage rise to 6.93x, and free cash flow after the USD 85.0 million dividend would shrink below the USD 65.6 million trailing level, which stops net debt from falling. Liquidity of USD 635.8 million covers debt service of USD 151.4 million for the first year, so there is no liquidity distress, but the 2028 notes of USD 583.7 million exceed the undrawn revolver by USD 121.3 million, and refinancing the notes at a higher coupon would add USD 38.7 million of interest. Management levers are advertising and capital expenditure, restructuring savings and the dividend and repurchases; the dividend is about USD 85.0 million a year. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA below USD 175.8 million, revolver borrowings above USD 30.0 million, collection of the remaining refund, and the first news of the 2028 refinancing. Primary downside path: margin erosion cuts earnings and cash flow before the 2028 refinancing, raising leverage and the cost of replacing the notes. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Energizer presents an average but pressured business profile supported by scale, established brands, low capital intensity and adequate liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 7.70x reported and 5.50x adjusted EBITDA, falling earnings that rely on add-backs, a tariff refund and a production credit, and a maturity wall in which USD 2,117.2 million of notes fall due in 2028 and 2029. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow swung between 10.95% and 99.79% of reported EBITDA and leaves little after the dividend. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on fiscal 2026 results meeting the USD 580 million guide, on collection of the refund, and on a coupon near the 6.00% of the 2033 notes. The primary downside path is margin erosion before the 2028 refinancing. Further analysis would require the fiscal 2026 results, the financing documents, the cash held by the U.S. borrowers, a rating and market spreads. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 notes on weaker earnings at a higher coupon. spans.text: ## Request

Source readiness for Energizer Holdings, Inc. (issuer id enr-1632790) as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the eight supplied filings and earnings releases support the requested work (financial foundation, business and governance, fundamental credit) and which other credit work they cannot support.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied Energizer filings and releases support a reported-financials credit snapshot through the quarter ended 2026-06-30, but not covenant, collateral, recovery or market-pricing conclusions, and nothing after 2026-08-04 is supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

A creditor cannot read its protections from these documents. The credit agreement and the note indentures appear only as exhibit references, the debt note describes the covenants as customary and says the company was in compliance, and no rating, price or portfolio input is supplied. The latest quarter-end covered is 141 days before the as-of date, so the fiscal 2026 year-end position is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 157–160; calculation C02
### Key findings

Coverage is strong for reported financials. The set holds the audited annual reports for fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025, the three quarterly reports of fiscal 2026 and the three matching earnings releases, so statements, segment results, the debt note and the company's non-GAAP reconciliations can each be traced to a supplied document. The quarterly reports carry prior-year quarter and year-to-date comparatives, but not prior-year interim balance sheets.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 104–106; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 99–101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

The debt picture is complete enough to rebuild the capital structure from the filings. At the latest quarter-end the debt note lists a secured term loan due 2032, four series of senior notes and capital leases, and the revolving facility due 2030 is described separately. The note's balances add to USD 3,327.3 million, and to USD 3,278.6 million once USD 48.7 million of capital leases is removed, which agrees to the stated schedule of maturities. Balance-sheet debt of USD 3,335.6 million agrees to the earnings release.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C03; calculation C04

One liquidity input is contradicted between filings. The latest quarterly report says USD 30.0 million was drawn on the revolving facility at both 2026-06-30 and 2025-09-30, while the 2025 annual report and the two earlier quarterly reports say nothing was drawn at 2025-09-30, and the same quarterly report's own notes-payable paragraph attributes the 2025-09-30 balance to other borrowings. The conflict is carried forward unresolved. Availability of USD 462.4 million at 2026-06-30 is consistent with a USD 500.0 million facility, USD 30.0 million drawn and USD 7.6 million of letters of credit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C05

The legal and structural modules cannot run on this set. Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control and Recovery & fulcrum all need executed documents, and the filings list the credit agreement, five indentures and four supplemental indentures dated 2026-01-02 only as exhibits incorporated by reference. Ratings & triggers, Security selection, Market-implied risk, Peer benchmark and Committee decision need a rating, quotes, peers or a portfolio, none of which is supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 157–160; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 55
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary point is that the filings are largely self-consistent: the debt note foots, the balance sheet agrees to the earnings release, and the revolver wording is the only difference found in the checks made here. That makes a reported-financials snapshot reliable as far as it goes. It does not make it a lender's view, because the company's own measures may differ from covenant definitions. The view would improve if the executed documents or the fiscal 2026 annual report were supplied, and would weaken if further differences between the annual and quarterly reports surfaced when the statements are read in full.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17
### Limitations

- Nothing dated after 2026-08-04 is supplied, so the fiscal 2026 year-end position, fourth-quarter results and any later financing are not established, and the company's own fiscal 2026 outlook cannot be tested against actual results.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C06

- No executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so covenant levels, guarantors, collateral and the permitted receivables financing cannot be read, and any statement about creditor protection rests on the filings' summaries.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 157–160; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18

- EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA figures are the company's own non-GAAP measures, printed only in the earnings releases and not in the filed reports, so any leverage or coverage ratio built on them follows the company's definition, not a lender's.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; EX99.1_2025-12-31_enr_enrpr123125-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Material: No executed financing document is supplied. The filings list the credit agreement's amendment and restatement agreement of 2025-03-19 and Amendment No. 1 of 2025-09-22, five indentures and four supplemental indentures dated 2026-01-02 as exhibits incorporated by reference. Covenant levels, guarantor lists, collateral, the receivables financing basket and call terms therefore cannot be read, and the debt note says only that covenants are customary and that the company was in compliance at 2026-06-30. The documents themselves would close this.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 157–160; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18

- Minor: The latest quarterly report says USD 30.0 million was drawn on the revolving facility at both 2026-06-30 and 2025-09-30, but the 2025 annual report and the two earlier quarterly reports say nothing was drawn at 2025-09-30, and the latest report's own notes-payable paragraph attributes the 2025-09-30 balance to other borrowings. Both versions are kept; availability at 2026-06-30 is unaffected. Issuer confirmation of the 2025-09-30 position would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C05

The company's definitions are not covenant definitions.
Basis: EX99.1_2025-12-31_enr_enrpr123125-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

- Minor: Prior-year interim balance sheets are not supplied, since the quarterly reports compare only with 2025-09-30. Cash interest and taxes paid are printed for fiscal years only, and the balance of receivables sold without recourse is printed only at fiscal year-ends (USD 144.4 million at 2025-09-30). Trends between year-ends and interim cash coverage therefore cannot be built from the filings alone.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 106, 151

- Minor: No rating, market quote, peer set, portfolio workbook, prior case, management bridge or research question is supplied, and the filings state no rating level. Work that depends on them is conditional until they are provided.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35

- Minor: Directors, ownership and executive pay are incorporated by reference from a proxy statement that is not supplied, so board composition and ownership percentages are not established; the executive officers' backgrounds are printed.

- Minor: Fiscal 2024 and 2023 net sales by market were recast in the 2025 annual report to show global professional markets separately, so market splits in the 2024 annual report differ in presentation from the later one. Both are kept and the later presentation is the one to use for fiscal 2024 comparisons.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Reported leverage rose over the nine months, narrowing the cushion beneath creditors: net debt of USD 3,162.2 million is 7.70x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-06-30, against 5.54x at 2025-09-30, because net debt barely fell while trailing EBITDA dropped.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C02; calculation C05

The issuer's adjusted EBITDA fell much less, from USD 623.6 million to USD 575.4 million, putting adjusted net leverage at 5.50x at 2026-06-30 against 5.12x at 2025-09-30, so most of the reported deterioration comes from items the issuer treats as one-off. The declared dividend adds USD 20.5 million of net debt, or 7.75x pro forma, and the tariff refund received after quarter end lowers it by USD 11.0 million, or 7.67x pro forma, each taken alone. Fiscal 2025 cash interest cover was 3.83x on reported EBITDA, and interim cover is not established because interim cash interest paid is not printed.

### Financial interpretation

Net debt rose by USD 204.7 million during fiscal 2025 and has eased by USD 33.3 million since, so the leverage swings come mainly from the EBITDA denominator rather than from borrowing. Net leverage on reported EBITDA was 9.00x at 2024-09-30, 5.54x at 2025-09-30 and 7.70x at 2026-06-30. Fiscal 2024 reported EBITDA of USD 332.4 million carried a USD 110.6 million intangible impairment, fiscal 2025 reported EBITDA of USD 577.2 million benefited from USD 78.0 million of retroactive production credits, and the trailing figure of USD 410.9 million carries USD 99.6 million of restructuring cost and a USD 26.3 million pension settlement loss.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2024-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 104–105; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C05

The issuer's adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 623.6 million to USD 575.4 million, which gives net leverage of 5.12x and 5.50x. The add-backs the issuer applies rose from USD 46.4 million to USD 164.5 million, so USD 118.1 million of the USD 166.3 million fall in reported EBITDA reflects higher add-backs rather than lower adjusted earnings. The strongest contrary evidence is that the adjusted view flatters the latest figure: it keeps USD 64.1 million of tariff refund benefit recorded in the nine months to 2026-06-30, only about USD 11.0 million of which had been collected after quarter end, and excluding that benefit alone would put adjusted net leverage at 6.18x (Analyst Judgement, not an issuer figure). A fourth-quarter result without further add-backs would favour the adjusted view; further restructuring cost or a delay in refund collection would favour the reported one.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C06; calculation C13

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 3.83x in fiscal 2025 against 2.26x in fiscal 2024, and adjusted EBITDA covered it 4.14x in fiscal 2025. Accrued interest expense was USD 118.1 million in the nine months to 2026-06-30 against USD 114.0 million a year earlier, but cash interest paid is printed for fiscal years only, so trailing cover at 2026-06-30 is not established and accrued expense is not substituted for it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 151; 10-K_2024-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 158; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 2

Operating cash flow was USD 147.1 million in fiscal 2025 against USD 429.6 million in fiscal 2024. Working capital absorbed USD 140.2 million in fiscal 2025 after releasing USD 121.9 million in fiscal 2024, and the cash flow statement deducts USD 120.9 million of production tax credits recognised in earnings but not yet collected. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 63.2 million in fiscal 2025 while dividends and share repurchases took USD 176.8 million, so debt issuance net of repayments of USD 174.5 million funded the gap. In the nine months to 2026-06-30 free cash flow was USD 103.9 million, shareholder payouts were USD 69.9 million and debt repayments were USD 97.5 million, and operating cash flow excludes USD 67.1 million of tariff refund recognised but not collected.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C10; calculation C15; calculation C16

Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was USD 173.4 million of cash plus USD 462.4 million undrawn on the revolving facility, USD 635.8 million in all, against USD 8.6 million of debt maturing within a year. The schedule is back-loaded: USD 592.3 million falls in the second year and USD 1,542.1 million in the third, together 65.10% of contractual principal, so the 2028 and 2029 senior notes are the refinancing test rather than near-term liquidity, and the revolving facility runs to 2030. About 93% of the cash at 2026-06-30 was held outside the U.S. (76.6% at 2024-09-30 and 81.6% at 2025-09-30); the company says such balances are generally available without legal restrictions, but repatriation could carry tax cost or regulatory capital requirements, so net debt subtracts cash that may not be freely available to the U.S. borrower.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation C08; calculation C09

Two items fund working capital without appearing as debt. Supplier-financed obligations of USD 46.7 million sit inside accounts payable at 2026-06-30, and receivables sold without recourse stood at USD 144.4 million at 2025-09-30, a balance printed at fiscal year-ends only. A fall in supplier or bank appetite would raise net debt without any change in earnings, and the latest sold-receivable balance is not established.

## Gaps

- High: No covenant definition, level or executed agreement is supplied, so the issuer's EBITDA and debt measures cannot be tested against any lender definition and covenant headroom cannot be calculated; the debt note says only that covenants are customary and that the company was in compliance at 2026-06-30. The executed credit agreement and indentures would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 157–160

- High: Cash interest paid and cash taxes paid are not printed for the nine months to 2026-06-30 or the quarter, so interest cover at the latest balance-sheet date, any trailing coverage and cash tax conversion cannot be stated; accrued interest expense is not substituted. A cash flow supplement for the interim periods would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 151; calculation C05

- High: No document after 2026-08-04 is supplied, so fiscal 2026 year-end balances, fourth-quarter EBITDA and any later financing are not established, and every balance in the set is at least 141 days old at the as-of date. The fiscal 2026 annual report would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Medium: The latest quarterly report says USD 30.0 million was drawn on the revolving facility at 2025-09-30 as well as 2026-06-30, whereas the annual report, the first two quarterly reports and the balance sheet indicate nothing was drawn; both versions are kept and nil is used. Issuer confirmation would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C09

- Medium: Fiscal 2024 adjusted EBITDA is not printed, so fiscal 2024 adjusted leverage and cover are not calculable and no house adjustment is constructed. A fiscal 2024 adjusted EBITDA schedule would close this.
Basis: EX99.1_2025-12-31_enr_enrpr123125-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2024-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 104–106

- Medium: The issuer's adjusted EBITDA includes tariff refund benefit and fiscal 2025 production credits, and the cash character, recurrence and collection timing of its add-backs are not itemised, so sustainable-earnings normalisation is restricted to a labelled sensitivity. Component support would close this.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C13

- Medium: Carrying values by instrument, security, ranking, guarantor scope, margins and floors are not stated for most debt instruments, so the debt stack carries only the two senior secured credit agreement facilities and secured and unsecured allocations are not established. The executed documents would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 137–138

- Medium: About 93% of cash at 2026-06-30 was held outside the U.S., and the company says repatriation could have adverse tax consequences or be subject to regulatory capital requirements, so the amount of cash readily available to the U.S. borrower and note issuers is not established and net debt subtracts all of it. A split of cash by entity and jurisdiction would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 103

- Medium: Receivables sold without recourse are printed at fiscal year-ends only, so the interim balance and the trend of this off-balance-sheet funding are not established; supplier-financed obligations are printed at each date. The interim balance would close this.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 19

- Medium: The nine months to 2025-06-30 comparative includes out-of-period production credits recorded in the third quarter of fiscal 2025, so year-on-year comparisons of that period are distorted; the credits are shown as separate figures. The issuer's quarterly schedules let the credits be isolated.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 41
- Low: Capital expenditure is printed as a total only, so maintenance and growth capex are not established and the free cash flow shown is not split between them.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3
- Low: No separate short-term investment balance is printed, since cash equivalents include marketable securities of three months or less, so no investment is added to or excluded from net debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 103

- Low: Source dashes in the statements (for example asset sale proceeds in fiscal 2025 and the third-quarter loss on extinguishment) are kept as missing rather than zero, which leaves component sums of those lines uncertified; reported totals remain usable.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3
- Low: Prior-year interim balance sheets are not supplied, so balance-sheet trends before 2025-09-30 other than the two fiscal year-ends are not available from the filings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- Low: No EBITDA figure is printed in the filed reports and no full-year fiscal 2025 EBITDA is printed in any release, so annual EBITDA is calculated from statement lines and checked against the printed quarters.
Basis: EX99.1_2025-12-31_enr_enrpr123125-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 99–101

- Low: The issuer prints no operating income line, so EBIT is not calculable, and no consistent quantified operating series (volumes, distribution points or customer retention) or prior-year nine-month organic growth rate is printed; management gives only percentage contributions to organic growth.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 44
- Low: Fiscal 2024 and 2023 net sales by market were recast in the fiscal 2025 annual report; no market split is used here and totals are unchanged.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 113

spans.text: ## Request

Business and governance fact base for Energizer Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, financial policy, capital allocation and the dated transactions and events in the supplied filings and releases.
## Sources

No external sources were used. Document dates are the dates the documents print on their signature pages or release headers.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance risk to creditors is medium and comes from financial policy rather than an owner: the company is widely held with no sponsor or controlling holder named, but fiscal 2025 shareholder payouts exceeded free cash flow in a year of net new debt financing.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation C03; calculation C08

Payouts of USD 176.8 million were 2.80 times free cash flow of USD 63.2 million in fiscal 2025, but in the nine months to 2026-06-30 payouts of USD 69.9 million were 0.67 times free cash flow of USD 103.9 million while the company repaid a net USD 83.5 million of debt. Project Momentum, now in a fourth year, has raised its restructuring cost range to USD 65.0 million to USD 75.0 million, so margin recovery is still being paid for. Ownership percentages, board detail and the executed financing documents are not supplied, so the risk level is provisional.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C03; calculation C08
### Key findings

The business is a mature, seasonal battery franchise whose growth was bought with price. Batteries were 76.11% of fiscal 2025 net sales and North America 55.88%, one retailer supplied 12.8% of sales, and fiscal 2025 organic growth of 0.7% combined volume growth of 1.5% with pricing declines of 2.2%. In the nine months to 2026-06-30 organic sales fell 2.3%, so earnings depend on cost savings rather than growth.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C01; calculation C02

Margins are the central operating risk. Segment profit fell 9.46% to USD 425.7 million in the nine months to 2026-06-30, with Auto Care down 26.82% and Batteries & Lights down 5.92%, and gross margin was 36.9% reported and 39.2% adjusted against 43.8% and 41.9% a year earlier, driven by unfavourable mix and production inefficiencies and cushioned by a USD 64.1 million tariff refund benefit that may not repeat. Lower segment profit shrinks the cash available to service debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 44–46; calculation C06

Restructuring has become a recurring charge, not a one-off. Project Momentum cost USD 59.7 million, USD 91.7 million and USD 68.7 million in fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025 and USD 76.8 million in the nine months to 2026-06-30, and its year-four range rose from a band of USD 35.0 million to USD 40.0 million to a band of USD 65.0 million to USD 75.0 million. Management reports about USD 206 million of savings, which is management language and not independently evidenced, so adjusted earnings that add these costs back depend on a programme that keeps recurring.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C05

Ownership is public and dispersed, so the creditor question is the Board's financial policy, not a sponsor's. No sponsor, controlling holder, owner fee or related-party leakage appears in the supplied pages, nine directors sign the annual report including an independent chairman, shares outstanding fell 4.85% between the November 2024 and November 2025 cover dates, and takeover protections make a leveraged change of control less likely. The absence of evidence is not evidence of absence, because the proxy statement that carries ownership and pay detail is not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 162; calculation C04

Capital allocation swung from shareholder-heavy in fiscal 2025 to deleveraging in fiscal 2026. Payouts exceeded free cash flow by USD 113.6 million in fiscal 2025, a year of USD 155.9 million of net new debt financing, whereas in the nine months to 2026-06-30 payouts were 0.67 times free cash flow, USD 90.0 million of term loan was prepaid and net debt financing was a repayment of USD 83.5 million. Acquisitions stayed small at USD 44.8 million across three bolt-ons, so they add integration risk rather than leverage.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C03; calculation C07; calculation C08

Disclosure supports monitoring of reported performance but not of lender protections. The audited annual report with effective internal control, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases are regular, yet covenants are described only as customary with compliance stated without levels, and the executed credit agreement, the indentures and the four supplemental indentures dated 2026-01-02 are not supplied, so the company's legal capacity to pay shareholders or add debt cannot be separated from its willingness.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 154; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a higher risk level is that fiscal 2025 payouts of USD 176.8 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 63.2 million, in a year when net new debt financing was USD 155.9 million, which would be creditor-adverse if repeated without covenant limits that cannot be seen. The strongest evidence for a lower level is that fiscal 2026 payouts fell to 0.67 times free cash flow, USD 90.0 million of term loan was prepaid, maturities were extended to 2030, 2032 and 2033, and no sponsor, fee or related-party leakage appears in the supplied pages. The view would move to low if the fiscal 2026 annual report shows continued repayment and the executed documents show tight restricted-payment limits, and to high if payouts again exceed free cash flow or the supplemental indentures show weaker note priority.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 137–138; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C03; calculation C08
### Limitations

- Ownership percentages, board committee detail and pay sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the finding of dispersed ownership rests on a count of holders of record and cover-page share counts, and the governance risk level stays provisional.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 156

- The purpose and terms of the four supplemental indentures dated 2026-01-02 are not in the supplied documents, so whether guarantor coverage or note priority changed, which would alter the reading of the financing behaviour, is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 55

- The funding of fiscal 2025 payouts is inferred from the cash flow statement, not stated payment by payment, so reading the payouts as met from new borrowing is an inference and could overstate the link.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 76; calculation C08
- Project Momentum savings and tariff mitigation are management statements without independent support, so the margin-recovery finding rests on management language rather than evidenced results.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 37

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Two financings in fiscal 2025 reshaped the debt without changing leverage. In March 2025 the credit agreement was amended and restated, extending the USD 760 million senior secured term loan to 2032 and the USD 500 million revolving facility to 2030 for debt issuance costs of USD 8.0 million. In September 2025 the company issued USD 400.0 million of 6.00% senior notes due 2033, guaranteed on an unsecured basis by certain domestic restricted subsidiaries, redeemed USD 300 million of 6.50% notes due 2027 with a premium of USD 4.9 million, and added USD 100.0 million to the term loan to repay revolver borrowings. Together the fiscal 2025 financings cost USD 13.6 million of debt issuance costs plus the premium, and extended the note maturity wall at a lower coupon.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 137–138; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 160

Acquisitions have been small and cash-funded: the APS business in Europe for USD 16.7 million, Centralsul in Brazil for a preliminary USD 16.5 million including an earnout, and Belgian battery assets for USD 11.6 million. In the nine months to 2026-06-30 the company prepaid USD 90.0 million of the term loan, completed the buy-out of the U.K. pension plan with a non-cash settlement loss of USD 26.3 million, and extended Project Momentum to a fourth year. Four supplemental indentures dated 2026-01-02 are listed as exhibits but their terms are not supplied, and the governing credit agreement and indentures are not in the supplied documents.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C07

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of Energizer Holdings, Inc. (issuer id enr-1632790) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business and financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring triggers on the supplied filings and earnings releases through the quarter ended 2026-06-30, read with the three earlier accepted analyses.

No external sources were used. Document dates are the dates the documents print on their signature pages or release headers.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Energizer's credit profile is weak: leverage is high, earnings are falling and partly supported by items that may not repeat, and creditors depend on refinancing USD 2,117.2 million of notes that fall due in 2028 and 2029. Liquidity of USD 635.8 million against USD 8.6 million of debt due within a year means the first test is refinancing, not a cash shortfall, and the 2028 notes fall due no later than 590 days after the as-of date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 47; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03; calculation C08; calculation C09

The assessment would improve if the guided fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 580 million is met with smaller add-backs and the 2028 notes are refinanced early, and worsen if the tariff refund goes uncollected or margins keep falling.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C02; calculation C03
### Key findings

Leverage is high and the adjusted measure flatters it. Net debt was USD 3,162.2 million at 2026-06-30, which is 7.70x trailing reported EBITDA and 5.50x the company's adjusted EBITDA. Pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-09-09, net debt is USD 3,182.7 million and 7.75x; pro forma for part of the tariff refund received after quarter end, with the receipt date not stated, it is USD 3,151.2 million and 7.67x; pro forma adjusted leverage is not established. Add-backs of USD 164.5 million are 28.59% of trailing adjusted EBITDA, against 7.44% in fiscal 2025, and the adjusted figure includes a USD 64.1 million tariff refund benefit, without which adjusted net leverage would be 6.18x.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C01; calculation C02

Margins are the weakest dimension. Adjusted gross margin fell 2.7 percentage points to 39.2% in the nine months to 2026-06-30 and reported gross margin fell 6.9 percentage points to 36.9%, as unfavourable mix and higher input costs from production inefficiency, with heavier promotion in the third quarter, more than offset the tariff refund benefit. Segment profit fell 9.46% to USD 425.7 million, a margin of 19.74% against 22.18%, and Auto Care shows the pattern: organic sales rose 9.5% in the third quarter, yet segment profit fell 14.1% because refrigerant growth carries a lower margin. Adjusted EBITDA for the nine months fell 10.65% to USD 404.2 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 44–46; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C03; calculation C04

The company's own guidance has moved down. In May management guided fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA to the high end of USD 580 million to USD 610 million; in August it guided to the low end, a cut of up to USD 30 million or 4.92%. At USD 580 million, adjusted EBITDA would be 6.99% below fiscal 2025 and the fourth quarter would need USD 175.8 million, 2.69% above the prior-year quarter, with organic sales guided flat to down. Management attributes the improvement to productivity and supply chain actions, and the fourth year of Project Momentum had realised about USD 15 million of savings and USD 8 million of cost avoidance by 2026-06-30, against USD 20.0 million to USD 25.0 million and USD 10.0 million to USD 15.0 million expected. Source readiness quoted the original range; the August release moved the guide to its low end.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_enr_enrpr33126-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 37; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C03; calculation C16

Free cash flow is positive but volatile and leaves little for debt reduction after the dividend. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 331.7 million in fiscal 2024, USD 63.2 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 150.6 million over the twelve months to 2026-06-30, which is 99.79%, 10.95% and 36.65% of reported EBITDA. After trailing dividends of USD 85.0 million, USD 65.6 million remains, enough to repay only 2.07% of net debt a year. The nine-month rise in operating cash flow to USD 156.0 million came from working capital, an outflow of USD 2.2 million against USD 133.5 million a year earlier; before working capital, operating cash flow fell 27.80% to USD 158.2 million from USD 219.1 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-K_2024-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 106; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07

The 2028 and 2029 maturities are the decisive test. The senior notes due in 2028 and 2029 total USD 2,117.2 million and the second and third years of the debt ladder hold 65.10% of contractual principal, while only USD 8.6 million falls due in the next twelve months. The 2028 notes of USD 583.7 million fall due between 2027-10-01 and 2028-06-30 and exceed the undrawn revolver of USD 462.4 million by USD 121.3 million, so repaying them from liquidity would use the whole revolver and cash that is mostly held abroad. Refinancing the three series at the 6.00% coupon of the company's 2033 notes, an illustration and not a forecast, would add USD 38.7 million of annual interest, 25.70% of trailing free cash flow. The 2025 refinancing, which replaced USD 300 million of 2027 notes with USD 400.0 million of 2033 notes and extended the bank facilities to 2030 and 2032, shows market access, but no financing document is supplied, so any springing maturity on the bank debt is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 137–138; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10

Liquidity is adequate for the next two years but thinner in the United States than the headline suggests. Liquidity was USD 635.8 million at 2026-06-30: cash plus USD 462.4 million undrawn on the USD 500.0 million revolver after USD 30.0 million of borrowings and USD 7.6 million of letters of credit; the revolver was undrawn at 2026-03-31, so the borrowing came in the third quarter, when free cash flow was about nil. It covers the next twelve months of scheduled principal and contractual interest, USD 151.4 million, 4.20 times. About 93% of cash was held outside the United States, which leaves roughly USD 12.1 million in it, so domestic liquidity is mostly the revolver, which runs to 2030. The company states that it complied with its covenants and expects to remain in compliance for twelve months, but no covenant level is printed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX99.1_2026-03-31_enr_enrpr33126-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C09; calculation C23

The business profile is average at best: the franchise is mature, concentrated and under pricing pressure. Trailing net sales of USD 2,989.1 million come mostly from batteries, 76.11% of fiscal 2025 sales, and from North America, 55.88%, where nine-month sales fell 2.93%; one retailer accounts for 12.8% of sales; and competition from private label and e-commerce is described as aggressive. Fiscal 2025 pricing declined 0.8% against volume growth of 1.5%, which corrects Business & governance, whose figure of 2.2% was the fiscal 2024 decline. The issuer's own accounting points to weaker brand value: the Rayovac trade name, carried at USD 337.0 million, was moved to a 30-year definite life after the quarter citing lower forecast demand and more competition, following USD 110.6 million of trade name impairments in fiscal 2024. Goodwill and intangibles are 45.12% of assets and exceed equity of USD 203.2 million by USD 1,812.0 million, so the asset value behind the debt is brand value.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 17; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C19; calculation C20

Financial policy is a moderate concern that improved in fiscal 2026. Shareholder payouts of USD 176.8 million in fiscal 2025 were 2.80 times free cash flow, in a year of net new borrowing, whereas nine-month payouts of USD 69.9 million in 2026 were 0.67 times free cash flow, USD 90.0 million of the term loan was prepaid and net debt was USD 33.3 million lower than at 2025-09-30. That improvement is smaller than it looks: net debt has risen by USD 47.8 million from USD 3,114.4 million at 2025-12-31, after the first quarter in which cash generation is seasonally strongest, and the revolver, undrawn at 2026-03-31, carried USD 30.0 million at 2026-06-30. The dividend of USD 0.30 per share a quarter was maintained, which with trailing free cash flow of USD 150.6 million leaves limited room if earnings fall further.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49; EX99.1_2025-12-31_enr_enrpr123125-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C06; calculation C17; calculation C23

The realistic downside is a margin squeeze that arrives before the refinancing, and liquidity would hold but not repay the 2028 notes. If the tariff refund went uncollected and the production credit were lost, trailing adjusted EBITDA would fall by USD 119.1 million to USD 456.3 million and adjusted net leverage would rise to 6.93x (Analyst Judgement, using the low end of the company's expected credit), which would make the refinancing harder and dearer while cash flow after the dividend shrinks.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14; calculation C15
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak assessment is that earnings still cover interest and liquidity is adequate. Trailing adjusted EBITDA is 4.03 times the next twelve months' contractual interest of USD 142.8 million and reported EBITDA is 2.88 times, no note matures before the 2028 notes, the company refinanced successfully in 2025, capital intensity is low at 2.24% of sales, and about USD 53.1 million of the tariff refund is still to be collected. The production credit, expected at USD 55 million to USD 65 million a year until its phase-out begins in 2030, is recurring rather than one-off, and the guided fourth quarter needs only USD 4.6 million more adjusted EBITDA than the prior-year quarter, against USD 7.0 million to USD 17.0 million of programme benefit still to be realised. The view would move toward average if fiscal 2026 results confirm adjusted EBITDA of USD 580 million or more with add-backs below USD 164.5 million, if adjusted net leverage returns to the 5.12x of 2025-09-30, if the refund is collected in cash and if the 2028 notes are refinanced early near the 6.00% coupon of the 2033 notes. It would weaken if adjusted EBITDA falls short of USD 580 million, add-backs rise again, free cash flow fails to cover the dividend as in fiscal 2025, revolver borrowings rise above USD 30.0 million, or the 2028 notes approach their final twelve months unrefinanced.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 50; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C21
### Limitations

- No rating, market price or peer set is supplied, so the judgement that the profile is weak is made against the issuer's own history and general leveraged consumer-products norms, not a measured peer range, and a stronger peer set could move it toward average.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 46

- The fiscal year ended on 2026-09-30, before the as-of date, so the forward view and downside rest on the August guide, which moved from the high end to the low end of its range, and results above or below it would change the conclusions on earnings and refinancing timing.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_enr_enrpr33126-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Without the credit agreement and indentures the refinancing timetable rests on stated maturities alone, and a springing maturity or a covenant tied to the 2028 or 2029 notes would bring the first test forward.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 138

- The refinancing cost of USD 38.7 million uses the company's own 6.00% coupon on the 2033 notes, not market yields, so a different yield at issue scales the cost and the share of free cash flow it takes.

- The production credit and tariff refund are management estimates, and the share of the credit inside trailing adjusted EBITDA is not printed, so the 9.56% to 11.30% exposure is a forward expectation against the trailing figure and not an actual share.

### Company description

Energizer makes and sells household and specialty batteries, portable lights and auto care products under the Energizer, Eveready and Rayovac brands, with Varta in Latin America and Asia Pacific, and Armor All, STP and A/C PRO in auto care. Sales go through mass merchants, food, drug, hardware, automotive and e-commerce channels, and about 40% of fiscal 2025 sales arose outside the United States. In the nine months to 2026-06-30, Batteries & Lights was 78.03% of segment net sales and Auto Care 21.97%. Battery demand follows device usage, consumer demographics and disasters and auto care follows the car parc and miles driven, so cash flow is needs-based but seasonal: batteries peak around the first fiscal quarter and auto care in the third and fourth, which makes working capital swing within the year. The business model supports debt service through steady replacement demand and low capital intensity, but it gives little pricing protection, because the sources give no backlog or customer contract term and sales depend on retailer shelf space.

Energizer is a listed Missouri corporation with no sponsor or controlling holder named and a dispersed holder base, so the financial-policy question is the Board's discretion over dividends and repurchases, which the company says depends on debt service obligations and covenants. Takeover protections in the articles and Missouri law make a leveraged change of control less likely. The credit agreement is guaranteed by certain domestic restricted subsidiaries, who also guarantee the 2033 notes on an unsecured basis; the guarantee scope of the 2028 and 2029 notes and the identity of the guarantors are not stated, and about 40% of sales and 93% of cash sit abroad, so claims on those assets may rank behind local liabilities. All figures are for Energizer Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries consolidated: no parent is named, so no parent figure is used, and Energizer Gamma Acquisition B.V. is a party to the euro notes' indenture without separate statements in the supplied documents. ### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is recurring in the sense that batteries and auto care products are replaced or topped up, but it is price-sensitive and moves with promotion. Organic growth was 0.7% in fiscal 2025, made of volume growth of 1.5% and pricing declines of 0.8%, then fell 2.3% in the nine months to 2026-06-30 as volumes fell 2.1% on softer U.S. consumer demand and a storm-heavy prior year, with pricing down 0.2%. The third quarter turned positive, with organic sales up 2.7% from volume gains of 4.1% against pricing declines of 1.4%, so recent volume has been bought with promotion. North America, 52.76% of nine-month sales, fell 2.93% in the nine months though it grew 4.31% in the third quarter. The largest customer, at 12.8% of fiscal 2025 sales, and the retailer trend toward private label limit pricing power; the expired acquired brand licence cut third-quarter sales by USD 17.2 million.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

The sources give no fixed-versus-variable cost split, but cost of products sold was 63.08% of net sales in the nine months to 2026-06-30, SG&A 19.09% and advertising 5.1%, and the plant network is being reshaped under Project Momentum. Principal inputs are manganese dioxide, zinc, silver, nickel, lithium, steel and plastic for batteries and refrigerant R-134a for auto care; zinc hedges cover a notional of about USD 24 million against nine-month cost of products sold of USD 1,360.3 million, so on the information supplied most input-cost and tariff exposure is not hedged and passes to margin unless priced. Margins have not been defended: adjusted gross margin fell 2.7 percentage points on mix, input cost and production inefficiency, partly offset by the tariff refund. Cost flexibility exists in advertising, which fell 6.55% to USD 109.9 million, and in the programme's savings of about USD 15 million in the first nine months of its fourth year, but both are modest against the margin loss.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is low: capital expenditure was 2.24% of trailing net sales, and USD 60 million to USD 70 million is planned for fiscal 2026, down from USD 75 million to USD 85 million in the annual report, of which USD 25 million to USD 35 million is Project Momentum, which shows capital expenditure being flexed. Conversion of reported EBITDA to free cash flow was 99.79% in fiscal 2024, 10.95% in fiscal 2025 and 36.65% over the trailing twelve months, which indicates that working capital, production credit receipts and restructuring cash costs, not capital expenditure, decide cash conversion. Inventory of USD 747.8 million is down from USD 781.2 million after the plastic-free packaging build, supplier-financed obligations of USD 46.7 million sit inside payables and receivables sold without recourse stood at USD 144.4 million at 2025-09-30, so a withdrawal of supplier or bank funding would raise net debt without any change in earnings. Seasonality concentrates cash generation in the first quarter: free cash flow was USD 124.2 million in that quarter and USD 105.9 million after six months.

### Competitive forces

Competitive rivalry is intense and mature: the annual report calls the categories highly competitive, names competitors with greater resources and describes aggressive competition in the United States, so promotion and price investment cap margin recovery and weigh on cash flow. The threat of new entrants comes mainly from retailers' private label and from e-commerce and discounters, which the company expects to shift consumption between channels and which can force lower prices or loss of distribution. Substitutes are not described beyond private label, so no further credit effect is claimed. Buyer power is high: customers frequently seek pricing concessions and better trade terms, one retailer is 12.8% of sales, and retailer consolidation is cited, which supports the view that pricing is a structural margin headwind. Supplier power is moderate: raw materials are commodities with fluctuating prices but available from several sources, and the company hedges part of its zinc, so supplier power matters mainly through tariffs and input-cost swings.

### Macro, policy and trade factors

Policy and trade factors are material to credit; social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. On the political and regulatory side, the Supreme Court held the IEEPA tariffs invalid on 2026-02-20, which created a refund claim of about USD 64 million that lifted nine-month earnings by USD 64.1 million while only about USD 11.0 million had been received after quarter end and the timeline for the rest is unclear; replacement tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on some trading partners keep the cost exposure open. The federal production credit, expected at USD 55 million to USD 65 million a year, depends on continuing regulation and phases out from 2030, so a change in policy would cut earnings directly. On the economic side, U.S. consumer demand is soft, currency moves reduce margin when local currencies weaken because much product cost is dollar-linked, and floating-rate debt of USD 791.9 million carries interest-rate risk.

### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths. Scale of about USD 3.0bn of trailing sales with established brands supports retailer access and cash generation; capital intensity of 2.24% of sales leaves cash for debt service; liquidity of USD 635.8 million is adequate against near-term obligations; the 2025 refinancing extended the bank facilities to 2030 and 2032 and issued 2033 notes; and the dividend was held while USD 90.0 million of term loan was prepaid. Weaknesses. Adjusted EBITDA is falling and carries add-backs of USD 164.5 million; margins are eroding under mix, promotion and input costs; USD 2,117.2 million of notes mature in 2028 and 2029; batteries and North America dominate sales; and intangible assets exceed equity. Opportunities. Collection of the remaining tariff refund of about USD 53.1 million, early refinancing before the notes become current, savings from the fourth year of Project Momentum and growth in e-commerce and Auto Care distribution could each improve credit quality. Threats. A retailer moving shelf space to private label, loss of the production credit, higher replacement tariffs, rising floating-rate cost as the swap steps down, and an adverse outcome in the consolidated antitrust class actions, for which no accrual is recorded, could each weaken it.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The main supports are liquidity with no maturity before the 2028 notes, low capital intensity, a demonstrated ability to refinance in 2025 and a policy shift toward debt repayment in fiscal 2026. The main constraints are leverage of 7.70x reported and 5.50x adjusted, falling earnings quality with 28.59% of adjusted EBITDA made of add-backs, volatile free cash flow and the 65.10% concentration of maturities in two years. The trend is negative on earnings and neutral on debt: net debt is USD 33.3 million lower than at 2025-09-30 but USD 47.8 million above its level at 2025-12-31, and trailing reported EBITDA is 28.81% lower than in fiscal 2025 and the company has cut its guide. The datapoints that would make the opinion more definitive are the fiscal 2026 year-end results, covenant levels and springing-maturity terms, the share of cash available to the U.S. borrowers, interim cash interest paid, and a rating or market spread; none is supplied.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months, the supports are the guided fourth-quarter profit recovery, collection of the remaining tariff refund, the savings and tariff mitigation from the fourth programme year, and production credit of USD 55 million to USD 65 million a year; the pressures are flat-to-lower organic sales, promotional pricing, replacement tariffs, restructuring guided at USD 80 million to USD 95 million of cost for fiscal 2026, interest expense guided at USD 150 million to USD 160 million, the roll-off of the interest rate swap that fixes the benchmark on USD 500.0 million and steps down by USD 100.0 million each December to 2027-12-22, and the start of the 2028 refinancing. Over three to five years the maturity wall of 2028 and 2029 comes first, then the revolver in 2030, the production credit phase-out from 2030, and the term loan in 2032 and notes in 2033. Rayovac amortisation begins on 2026-07-01 but is non-cash. At the guided figures and with net debt held at its 2026-06-30 level, adjusted net leverage would be 5.45x and reported 7.42x, so the guide implies no deleveraging from earnings. Each pressure works through margin and refinancing cost, not liquidity, in the first two years.

### Downside scenario

The scenario starts with a continued consumer slowdown and retailer promotion, set against higher replacement tariffs, which holds organic sales below the flat-to-down fourth-quarter guide. The first operational break is gross margin: adjusted gross margin would stay below the 39.2% of the nine months as mix and promotion offset savings, and the tariff refund of USD 64.1 million and the production credit stop supporting earnings. Financially, trailing adjusted EBITDA would fall to USD 456.3 million and adjusted net leverage rise to 6.93x, and free cash flow after the USD 85.0 million dividend would shrink below the USD 65.6 million trailing level, which stops net debt from falling. Liquidity of USD 635.8 million covers debt service of USD 151.4 million for the first year, so there is no liquidity distress, but the 2028 notes of USD 583.7 million exceed the undrawn revolver by USD 121.3 million, and refinancing the notes at a higher coupon would add USD 38.7 million of interest. Management levers are advertising and capital expenditure, restructuring savings and the dividend and repurchases; the dividend is about USD 85.0 million a year. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA below USD 175.8 million, revolver borrowings above USD 30.0 million, collection of the remaining refund, and the first news of the 2028 refinancing. Primary downside path: margin erosion cuts earnings and cash flow before the 2028 refinancing, raising leverage and the cost of replacing the notes.
