### Overall credit view

Overall, Energizer presents an average but pressured business profile supported by scale, established brands, low capital intensity and adequate liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 7.70x reported and 5.50x adjusted EBITDA, falling earnings that rely on add-backs, a tariff refund and a production credit, and a maturity wall in which USD 2,117.2 million of notes fall due in 2028 and 2029. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow swung between 10.95% and 99.79% of reported EBITDA and leaves little after the dividend. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on fiscal 2026 results meeting the USD 580 million guide, on collection of the refund, and on a coupon near the 6.00% of the 2033 notes. The primary downside path is margin erosion before the 2028 refinancing. Further analysis would require the fiscal 2026 results, the financing documents, the cash held by the U.S. borrowers, a rating and market spreads. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 notes on weaker earnings at a higher coupon.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C08; calculation C10; calculation C14
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main credit strengths are liquidity, cash needs and a record of refinancing. Liquidity of USD 635.8 million covers the next twelve months of scheduled principal and interest 4.20 times and no note matures before the 2028 notes, so near-term default risk is low. Capital expenditure is only 2.24% of trailing sales, and free cash flow after the dividend was USD 65.6 million, so ordinary operations were funded from cash flow over the trailing period. The 2025 issue of USD 400.0 million of 2033 notes and the extension of the bank facilities to 2030 and 2032 show that lenders and investors supported the credit when adjusted net leverage was 5.12x, below the 5.50x of today.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 137–138; calculation C06; calculation C09; calculation C12

The main weaknesses are the maturity wall, falling earnings and weak earnings quality. USD 2,117.2 million of notes mature in 2028 and 2029 and refinancing them at a higher coupon would add about USD 38.7 million a year, while trailing reported EBITDA fell 28.81% from fiscal 2025 and add-backs are 28.59% of adjusted EBITDA. Margin erosion is visible in both segments, and the tariff refund and production credit that support adjusted earnings may not repeat. Intangible assets exceed equity by USD 1,812.0 million, so asset value behind the debt is brand value that the issuer itself now forecasts lower.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C10; calculation C12

## Gaps

- Material: The fiscal year ended 2026-09-30 and the fourth-quarter results are not supplied, and the company has moved its adjusted EBITDA guide from the high end of USD 580 million to USD 610 million in May to the low end in August, so the forward view, leverage at year-end and the timing of the first refinancing step are not established. The fiscal 2026 annual report would close this.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_enr_enrpr33126-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C16

- Material: No credit agreement, indenture or supplemental indenture is supplied, so covenant levels, any springing maturity on the 2030 revolver or 2032 term loan, guarantor scope of the 2028 and 2029 notes and restricted-payment baskets are not established, and the refinancing timetable rests on stated maturities. The executed documents would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 138; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 55

- Material: No rating, market price or peer set is supplied, so the refinancing cost uses the company's own 6.00% coupon as a proxy and the relative position against peers is not measured. A rating report and quotes would close this.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; calculation C10

- Minor: Correction to Business & governance: fiscal 2025 pricing declined 0.8% against volume growth of 1.5%, giving organic growth of 0.7%; the figure of 2.2% in that analysis is the fiscal 2024 pricing decline. Its point that volume was helped by lower prices holds, but the fiscal 2025 price effect is smaller than stated there.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation C20

- Minor: Source readiness listed the fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook as the range of USD 580 million to USD 610 million; the August release places it at the low end and the May release placed it at the high end.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_enr_enrpr33126-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_enr_enrpr63026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Minor: The latest quarterly report says USD 30.0 million was drawn on the revolver at 2025-09-30 as well as 2026-06-30, whereas the annual report and the first two quarterly reports show it undrawn; this analysis follows the balance sheets, which show the revolver undrawn until 2026-03-31 and drawn at 2026-06-30, and the 2025-09-30 wording stays unresolved.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 138; 10-Q_2026-03-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2025-12-31_enr.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Minor: Interim cash interest paid is not printed, so cover is shown on the next twelve months' contractual interest of USD 142.8 million, which uses 2026-06-30 balances and rates and may differ from cash actually paid.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C11
- Minor: The share of cash held by the U.S. borrowers is estimated at about USD 12.1 million from the approximate 93% held abroad, and the cash by entity and jurisdiction is not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C09

- Minor: The production credit recognised in the trailing twelve months is not printed as a single figure, so the credit's share of adjusted EBITDA is shown only against the company's expected annual range.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-09-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation C14

- Minor: The benchmark rate at the time of the step-downs is not supplied, so the extra interest cost as the swap steps down from USD 500.0 million is not quantified, although the swap's unrealised gain is printed at USD 19.4 million at 2026-06-30.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_enr.htm.jsonl, page 52
